data.gender_notes: Sabriel is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Hebrew sab, meaning 'to protect' and riel, meaning 'god' or 'helper'. In the Bible, this name is associated with the prophet Zechariah and a priest named Sabriel. The name Sabriel carries the meaning “God of Sabre, or helper” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Sabriel usually hope their child will grow to embody god of sabre, or helper and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Sabriel belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “God of Sabre, or helper.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Sabriel total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

This name may be reflective of a deep respect and reverence for the power and protection that God can provide. The Hebrew roots of the name may also evoke a connection to the long and rich history of the Jewish people, and their deep spiritual traditions.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Sabriel holds spiritual significance as it evokes the idea of being protected and guided by God. The name is inspired by the Hebrew word 'sab' meaning to protect, and 'riel' meaning God. The name can serve as a reminder of the power and presence of God in our lives, offering a sense of comfort, security, and strength. The name Sabriel is a powerful reminder that God is our help and our refuge, always present and ready to protect and guide us. It is a name that can inspire a deep sense of faith and trust in God's protection and presence.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Sabriel, meaning "God is my strength" in Hebrew, symbolizes the deep faith and trust in the divine power that sustains us during life's trials. It is a reminder of God's presence in times of adversity, offering comfort and reassurance that He will carry us through.
